utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We'll be sitting today pursuant to Rule 15 bis, with Judge Baird being away due to his urgent matters. Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I remind you that your oath is still valid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We were in the middle of -- Mr. Gaynor, could you remind me whether or not you completed your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I haven't yet completed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We had just finished with the Safeta Zajke Street incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to turn to another incident, G7, in your statement at pages 14 and 15. You refer to your participation into an investigation into a case of three shells fired on Dobrinja 1 on the 4th of February, 1994. Do you recall your participation in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for P1739, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I believe you've already had an opportunity to inspect this map. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The location marked with a green digit "7" and a green dot, do you agree that that green dot marks the approximate midpoint of the impact locations of the three shells in this incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe briefly the nature of this part of Sarajevo where the shells landed.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a suburb of Sarajevo. The buildings there are up to five storeys high. This is an exclusively residential area. In other words, it's an urban settlement where you have buildings, schools, shops. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You prepared a sketch of the incident site; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 16802, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At the top, we see the legend to your sketch; is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And in the description at the bottom, we see the digits "02.04.1994." Is that a reference to the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That's the 4th -- the 4th of February, 1994. I made a mistake by mixing up the month and the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. We're agreed that's the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that the next page not be broadcast, but that it be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page, we see your signature and the date, 14th of the 11th, 1995. Now, is it correct that you signed that when you met with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, and you signed a copy of this sketch when providing a statement on that date?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: According to the legend you provided on the previous page, the locations 1, 2 and 3 mark the impact locations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I understand you wish to make a correction to the direction marked "North" on this sketch. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that the sketch be rotated 180 degrees, please. I now propose to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's okay as it is, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Could I provide, please, the witness with a hard copy of the map that he's just inspected, which is page 10 of the Sarajevo-specific court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: First of all, does the street marked on this sketch Ulica Oslobodilaca Grada, is that the same as Oslobodilaca Sarajeva; could you confirm that, first of all?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, would it assist if we rotated the map -- the sketch 180 degrees? Would that help you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's all right as it is. Shall I mark --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could mark the direction north on the map now, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The arrow points in the direction north; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And if you could sign and date that sketch.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And if that could be admitted under seal, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why do we have to put it under seal? Why have you asked him to sign his real name?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It already contains a copy of his signature on this page. That was why I was requesting him -- he can simply give his witness number, if Your Honours wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1802, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll now move to another incident, which is Incident G-15.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, at pages 13 and 14 -- there's no need to consult the map now for the moment -- you refer to an incident at Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva on the 16th of June, 1995. Do you recall your participation in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we move on, Mr. Gaynor, I wonder whether the witness would be able to explain why he made a mistake when he first drew this sketch. Could you answer that, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time when I was making the first sketch, we were under large pressure because nine people were killed and about another twenty were wounded as a result of this shelling, and our life was constantly in danger while we were conducting our on-site investigation because one is completely in the open while doing that, and this location is in close proximity to the front-line, and one can almost see very clearly -- or the aggressor could clearly see the point from the hill that they were holding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I leave it there. It's up to you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to call up, please, Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 13564, please. This is page 11 of the Sarajevo-specific court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, could you confirm that the green dot marked with the digit 11 on this -- I beg your pardon. The green dot marked with the digit 15 on this map is the impact location?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the impact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again, could you describe, briefly, the general nature of the impact area.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area is called Alipasino Polje, and it is a purely urban area, with residential buildings where people lived. There were also schools and shops. So as I said, an urban quarter of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I request that this map be admitted, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1803, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, you drew a sketch of the incident site; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 09819, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is the sketch of the incident location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page, please, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've marked a legend at the top of this, and the figures correspond with those on your sketch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In this sketch, could you just simply focus on the figures "1110 by 780," and explain what those figures refer to.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch and these figures represent the point of impact of the modified explosive device, and these sizes, 1110 times 780, is the size of the crater created by the modified explosive device.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you just clarify the units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is expressed in centimetres, so it's 1.110 centimetres by 780 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that the sketch be admitted under seal, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why under seal again, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again, the sketch contains a signature of the witness. I will prepare public versions of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The under-seal version will be Exhibit P1804, and the public redacted version will be Exhibit P1805.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, you took photographs of the incident location; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 09792, please. If we could zoom in on photograph 1. This can be broadcast. Zoom in on the top photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe, in general terms, what this depicts.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see here the point of impact or the point where this projectile had landed and the hole it made in the concrete path that you can see further beyond. You can see it's made of concrete. And this path leads behind the building. You can see people standing on the edge of this crater, and you can also see how small the people are in comparison to the size of the crater. You can see how big it is. Another important point is you can see a corner of this building next to which the projectile landed, and this building had more than 10 storeys, so had it impacted on the building, it would probably have destroyed it completely. This is a residential building, just to add that, and there were at least four to five families living on each storey, so you can only imagine the number of casualties that might have been caused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please. Again, if we could zoom in on the top photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe what is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used number 1 and a scaler in order to mark the rocket motors that propelled this modified explosive device.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I request that this be admitted -- this exhibit could be admitted as a public exhibit, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1806, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And that ends the direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we dealt with the admitting exercise of associated exhibits, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you for the reminder, Mr. President. We have not. We can go through it now, if Your Honours wish. The associated exhibits which have already been admitted have been listed on page 5 of the appendix to the Rule 92 ter notification in respect of this witness. I can indicate that in the list, starting on page 2, the third exhibit should be admitted under seal, and otherwise the exhibits which were admitted under seal in the previous proceedings, we would move for them to be admitted under seal in these proceedings as well. They're all marked on the list. And those, with the exception that I've noted which were admitted publicly, can be admitted publicly in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, other than the one that deals with the unscheduled incident that I indicated previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One of the associated exhibits is a video-clip, which 65 ter number is 40086. Has it been up-loaded in the e-court? Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll confirm that. We have provided it to the Trial Chamber on a CD version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then they would be all admitted, and the exhibit numbers will be circulated to the parties in due course by the Court Deputy. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Witness, you will be asked further questions by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Good morning to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I begin, just for the sake of formality, I'd like to remind everyone that we have at least five major incidents to deal with, plus some general issues that pertain to the witness, himself. Therefore, it might again bring us into the situation that we are pressed for time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let me ask you straightforward about the 4th of February incidents, because it's fresh in your memory. That was in 1994. Did that happen one day before the major incident called "Markale 1"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that. And, believe me, I cannot remember all the dates from 16 years before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the amalgamated statement, it is stated in your answer that you were a forensic technician. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is your educational background? What do you need in order to become that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to acquire the status of a forensic technician, it is necessary to finish secondary engineering school. And after that, once you join the police, you have to attend a special police course, which I did, and which lasted six months. After that, you take an exam or a series of exams, and eventually you get the status of the criminal investigation technician or a forensic technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, in other words, can you tell me what would be the role of the forensic technician during an investigation? What is he exactly doing?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of investigation, a forensic technician is an individual who goes along with a group of investigators to the crime scene, and his task, first and foremost, is of a technical nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is he doing, exactly?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His first task would be to photograph the scene, to draw a sketch of the scene, and prepare a forensic and criminal investigation report. He also collects all the evidence on the spot and hands it over to the investigations [as interpreted] and experts for further expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So all of this is done by him on the spot?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What he does on the spot is the bulk of the work that he has to do, and, of course, all the paperwork will have to be done in an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this something that's done with a ruler, these precise actions, or is this done in the office?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a rough sketch made on the site which is measured. The precise dimensions are entered, measured by a tape measure. Everything -- all the data is entered on the sketch. And then at the office, the actual sketch is made using a ruler, using the same measurements that were taken at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then everything is revised and the forensic report is drafted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no revision. What was observed on the scene is written in the criminal technical investigation report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if there's a mistake made, it's something that can be corrected in the office?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you cannot correct any errors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it important, the time and the actual situation on the scene? Is the time and the place of coming to the scene important?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best is to come to the scene of the incident immediately when the incident happens. Usually, we would come to the scene as soon as the police out in the field reports to us that an incident has taken place. Then a team is composed, headed by an inspector who is leading that group of people, and we go to the scene of the incident. If it's a more serious crime where there is a person who has been killed or injured, then an investigative judge and an investigator would also accompany or be part of the team, a doctor too, forensic experts would come also, because they are important when we are talking about this type of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is a rule during peacetime as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the procedure is the same during war and peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that you had additional training that focused on war crimes. What did that involve?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any additional training that would cover war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So then -- I have to wait for the interpretation. The incident that occurred during the war, did you treat them just like any other incident that occurred during peacetime?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you establish if there were any alterations or changes on the scene?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes we wouldn't immediately go to the scene of the incident. We would go a little later. And we would have to record that in the report, that we came to the scene later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a rule or an exception?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a rule to record such information. However, the rule was that we would immediately go to the scene of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. So the exception would be to go to the scene of the incident later?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We would only go later only in the case when there was intense shelling underway or when it was very dangerous to go to the scene. We would not wish to endanger the lives of the people in the investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And which part of the forensic report could we say was yours? Which part are you responsible for?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am responsible for the photographing -- the photographs taken at the scene, the diagram, and the criminal investigation technical report. However, it was my duty also to compile any traces and hand over any traces of the incident for testing and expert examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us: Why is it that in all of these incidents, we don't have any photographs or records of the victims? There is no sketch on the ground. There is no relational data. Why is there no such information in the reports for any of these cases?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. In peacetime, we would precisely mark the outline where the victim lay, in chalk. We would mark the position of the victim, the surrounding objects, the area. And the investigation at the scene would be conducted thoroughly, it would take a long time. However, when a shell strikes and kills all the people around at that location, those who survived automatically -- it's a question of survival. It's some kind of God's will to save the lives of people. Those people simply get up and they want to help those who are injured. They want to put them in cars and transport them to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the dead?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, everyone is taken to the hospital first, because you cannot establish with 100 per cent certainty who is dead and who is alive, because most of the shrapnel injuries are quite terrible. People are exposed to horrible lacerations and cuts, there is heavy bleeding. A piece of shrapnel would irregularly cut the human body. There would be lots of blood vessel injuries. So all the people are taken straight to the hospital, where the doctors try to help them. After that, if they survive, their treatment continues. If not, they are taken to the morgue, which is part of the hospital, the Kosevo Hospital or any other hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At one point in time here, you said -- perhaps this is the Trg Prijateljstva incident. You said that there were no dead bodies, but you did observe traces of blood.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When you come to the scene, you would see parts of bodies, you would see pools of blood, literally pools of blood; not dripping blood, but pools of blood. You would see pieces of the body parts, of the skull, bone fragments, body parts, parts of clothing, shoes. I mean, you really are aware that you are in a horrible place.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did photograph it; not everything, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Witness. The interpreters were not able to follow the question and answer because you are overlapping each other. Please, again, put a pause between the question and answer. The interpreters couldn't hear your question, Mr. Karadzic. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked, Why didn't you photograph that? And then the witness said, I did photograph it; not everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is something that is quite unclear to me, the quite obvious absence of these photographs in your forensic reports. Did IFOR [as interpreted] allow the scene to be disturbed so much that these elements are not shown or are missing from the photographs? Not "IFOR," I didn't say "IFOR." Did you permit -- did anyone permit; not IFOR, anyone? How did it happen that these photographs and, generally, these pieces of forensic evidence are so denuded that there are no key pieces of data; how many people were killed, relational aspects, the location of the bodies? Why is it that in peacetime this is something that you did thoroughly? You couldn't appear before a trial chamber without this complete forensic data, without sketches, without all the information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. However, I repeat, when such an incident takes place, when people all around are screaming and moaning, lying in pools of their own blood, the citizens who survived, who are close by, who are at the location, would try to help them, to transport them to the hospital as soon as possible in order for them to be given medical assistance so that they don't bleed to death. This is a very simple reason, because it's just a question of life and death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I completed my medical studies in Sarajevo, and all of my medical education, other than some parts of my psychiatric training, I completed all of that in Sarajevo. How is it that in your testimony, and even in footage, you could see the wounded and the dead being dragged? You said that you even saw traces of bodies being dragged. Where in the world does it happen that these bodies are dragged?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, I said that people are transferred to the closest vehicle and transported to the hospital, where medical assistance is given to them. So the point is to provide medical assistance to a wounded or injured person in order to prevent bleeding and to help that person survive. It's a -- it's a struggle to keep a person alive. These are minutes -- seconds involved that would decide whether somebody would survive or not. I mean, it's a question -- it's a matter of life and death. You're a doctor. You ought to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said that you saw bloody tracks of bodies being dragged along the ground, and we saw in video footage that people -- bodies were being dragged on the ground. So Sarajevo medicine would not permit such bad practices. Sarajevo medicine, the medicine practiced in Sarajevo, was good. Anyway, let's look at page 8 of this amalgamated statement, where you say that sometimes you would establish the directions approximately; you were not quite sure about the direction. Was direction established in these cases, and was the distance from which the projectile came also determined?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My primary task was not to establish the direction from which the projectile came, because this was something that was done more precisely by ballistics experts, people from the Counter-Sabotage Protection and forensic ballistics experts. So there are experts who were dealing with the direction from which the projectile came. I, personally, don't know that anyone was concerned with the distance covered by the projectile. This is something that I did not deal with. I didn't take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And these reports, including all the investigation material, was that something that made a complete whole, a set?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 11, line 20, you said that there were some official photographers. Other than yourself, were there any other people taking photographs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one else photographing, other than me, unless in some cases there were two technicians that came to the scene, so they helped each other. However, within our Criminal Investigation Department at the Sarajevo CSB, we had a person who filmed all the incidents with a camera. When this was necessary, he would make a camera recording at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned in a number of places here that, whenever possible, UNPROFOR was there. Did UNPROFOR also conduct their own investigations at the scene?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they did. They made their own notes and they gave their own findings and opinion about each individual incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And which incidents were filmed by video camera?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The video footage was made for incidents where there was a large number of casualties, where a large number of people were killed, where many people were killed. That's where the scene was filmed by video camera as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And for which of these incidents is there video footage?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you exactly which incidents, but I am sure that wherever there were a large number of victims, there was also video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm waiting for the interpreter as well. There was a large number of victims at the Dobrinja incident. Do you have video footage for that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Incident G-11 of the 24th of May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Majdanska Street, again on the 24th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question because I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva? Is there a video report on that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no such report for Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Hrasnica; is there a video footage of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also know nothing about Hrasnica. Trust me, this was not part of my remit, because I didn't follow it for that reason. And, again, as I say, it was 16 years ago, 17 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence fully agree that you look into your contemporaneous reports in order to assist you. Let me ask you this: Did you follow the testimony given by Mr. Sabljica which took place recently in this court?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. All I saw was on the news, that he appeared as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you consult with Mr. Sabljica afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't speak to him in any way whatsoever, nor did I consult with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's not forbidden. I'm just asking. Let's now move to the Dobrinja incident of the 4th of February, 1994. Do you know now why this report is wrong?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why the report is wrong, other than the wrongly-marked north, which I corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we have a new northerly direction. So if you change it from 90 degrees to some 30 or 40 degrees, does that affect the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. I did not plot the direction onto my sketch from which the shell came because that part of the work, that is, to establish the direction, was done by ballistic experts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have in e-court P1802, and I suppose it shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But they determined the direction from which it came based on the bearing measurements that they had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was there while they were doing their job, and they observed and reviewed the traces left by the explosion of a 120-millimetre shell. And based on these traces left on the concrete surface, they determined the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This should not be broadcast. Now, please focus on this. Can you see, in the left top corner, where it says "Zgrada," "Building"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's located in the south, and the point of impact is north of that building, according to what you marked?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you honestly, at that moment when we were doing all this, I was not familiar with that particular suburb of the city of Sarajevo. We had to conduct our investigation quickly and under tremendous pressure, so my duty was to take photographs, to draw a sketch, and just to pray to God not to be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we don't have to hurry. You did this in your office by using a ruler; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you did that on the basis of the sketch that you made on the spot?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So let's try and agree on this. The point of impact on the playground is on the northern edge of that playground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says number 1.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But would you say north from the edge? You have to tell me north from which particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If this is how you draw it, the diagonal of this playground, the bearing is approximately zero, viewed from north?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This line that you drew indicating north, can you transpond [as interpreted] it to the playground or draw another one in the playground so that we have a diagonal line in the playground placed facing north, and that at its northerly corner was the place where the shell fell?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This building above on the drawing, is it true that another shell, number 2 or whatever the sequence was, landed on its northerly side?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 3 fell on the westerly side of the building, itself?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the south side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you look at the axis of the building, it intersects with the northerly one?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But then it would be a diagonal. So number 3 is on the south.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D0291. I'm sorry, I'm really sorry. Can we have it back? The drawing, I mean. Can we have it back? P1802.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, can you mark here with an arrow the direction where Lukavica is situated?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I can't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lukavica should be approximately due south or south-east, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it now, then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly south?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps south, south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put the letter L to indicate "Lukavica," and after that we can admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we do that, Your Honours, under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I just noted that page 20 in B/C/S and page 11 in English of 65 ter 9617, which is a report of this incident, bears the same sketch without his signature, so I'm wondering why we have to admit all these marked maps under seal. But we'll do that in the meantime, we'll admit it under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D798, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why were you standing on the north and doing this sketch when it is customary to stand in the south and face north?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I don't believe there's any evidence that it was customary to stand in the south and face north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. Could you reformulate your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you standing there in the north and facing south when you were making this sketch?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made this sketch very quickly, and the first thing that I did was to draw the buildings in the space, how their layout is, including the garage and the streets. Only after that did I plot in the northerly direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the point where you stood?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, because the shells landed in a wide area. We're not talking about a few metres, we're talking about several hundreds of metres. So this is an entire complex of buildings that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the person making the drawing was standing where? Where were you standing when you imagined yourself in this space?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, but I did not indicate the standing point here, nor did I include it in the legend. And, again, I'm telling you the reason for that was because three shells landed at three different places several hundred metres apart; therefore, I did not make this sketch properly and include the standing point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did this in your office; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the majority of the work was done on the ground. And it is crucial that one makes a correct sketch on the spot, and then you use a ruler only to provide the description.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you use the city map of Sarajevo in doing so?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not even when you went back to your office?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You know, there were so many incidents that were happening one after another so quickly. We were under huge pressure, our lives were in danger, and this was a very stressful situation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 1D2191. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the street of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva, and do you agree that's 353?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see "353" anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this red dot. It's at Mimar Sinana Bulevar, and then it says "353" in the direction of the airport.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the interpreters couldn't hear your answer. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that at first glance, I couldn't find the street 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But now you can see it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to be assisted in order to draw some elements into this map; the garage, and everything that was happening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer this question because I didn't visit this location for 17 years. Therefore, I'm unable to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did provide an answer to the Prosecutor when he showed you something similar. Can you mark here the direction pointing at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the direction of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark north -- direction north along the Street 353?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did the incident happen; on the left- or the right-hand side of the street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that the incident took place on both sides of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say that on your sketch. There is a garage and so on. Can you please -- on which side of the street of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva was this playground as we look at it? Was it on the left- or the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that because I cannot recognise that place at all. I wasn't there for the past 17 years. I'm sorry, but I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street exits onto the Bulevar Mimar Sinana Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it does not touch the Hamdije Kapidzica Street at all?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And why does it then say in the statement that the incident occurred at the crossroads of Hamdije Kapidzica and Oslobodilaca Grada, as it says here? Is there a street called Oslobodilaca Grada?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you do have your report, please look at it. It says "Oslobodilaca Grada Street," and the Hamdije Kapidzica Street is also mentioned, the intersection of those two streets, which actually is not shown here.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the report in front of me. All I can say is that that day, I came to the scene, I quickly made a sketch, and I ran from there as far -- fast as my feet would carry me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now indicate on this map this erroneous direction of the north, which is to the -- which lays 90 degrees in relation to Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do that because I cannot make a connection between my diagram and this diagram that you are showing to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Then can you just put the initials -- actually, your number here, so that we don't have to tender this document under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your number is KDZ166.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In order to be fair, in your report it says "Ulica Oslobodilaca Sarajeva" and Dzavaharlal Nehru Street." So you agree that Hamdije Kapidzica Street was earlier called Jawaharlal Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if Hamdije Kapidzica Street was earlier called Jawaharlal Nehru Street, then that is the one that the report refers to?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I'm not familiar with the streets in that part of town at all. I have no idea how to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The marked map will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D799, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just wanted to note that Mr. Karadzic has not yet provided any information as to the date of the street pattern set out in this map. The date -- the map information set out in the Prosecution's map in relation to this incident dates from 1994, so I want to note for the record that there's no indication as to when this street pattern dates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Defence must have heard your submission, but can you answer that question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we showed the previous witness the list of old and new streets, and that Hamdije Kapidzica at an earlier map is Jawaharlal Nehru Street. At least, I think we established the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Instead of making submissions, look into the matter and come back with an answer later. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to note - we might as well clarify it now - there are two issues, one is the old and new street names. Mr. Karadzic's list which he's previously provided does not in fact agree with the Prosecution's list of old and new street names for Sarajevo. That's point number 1. Point number 2 is the street pattern, the actual layout of the streets. That's the point I was making. Mr. Karadzic hasn't provided information as to when this street pattern dates from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you remember that Dobrinja was originally the Olympic Village and that the streets and the buildings were completed in 1984? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know if any of these streets changed their position from 1984 to today?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I do know for a fact that the street names were changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We agree. Do you remember what was said in the report about where the shells came from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was said in the report that the shells came from the direction of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, which direction would that be?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be south-east.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when you marked it, Lukavica is to the south-east from that area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's north-east from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D0 -- actually, 65 ter 09617, please. It's an unsigned sketch. Actually, we would need to look at the signed sketch. This is P1802. I think that's better, the one that has the cardinal directions marked. P1802.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at number 2. There is a building there. Along the building, the front of the building, a grenade dropped. It should have arrived from the south-east. How could that shell have come from the south-east and impacted the very edge of the building? Did it pass through the building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It couldn't penetrate the building, the shell. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And knowing where the north is, can you now mark where south-east is? East is straight to the right from --

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How could this shell have come from the south-east and landed in front of the building that is several storeys high?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have come from the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the east, then, so that we can see?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did this shell land coming from above or over the garage? And what about this number 3; how could that have landed over this building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have impacted there without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put "S-E" for the direction of south-east and "E" for the direction of east?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So where is Lukavica here, then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I look at the other map now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you something. In the previous map, where there was the Lukavica road, it was easier for me to determine where Lukavica is. Now it's a little bit more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you said it was on the south-east. Is Lukavica in the south-east?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Lukavica is here in the east, east in Dobrinja. Actually, in relation to Dobrinja, Lukavica is in the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There seems to be a technical difficulty in the French translation. One of the Bench members is not receiving French translation. I note the time. Shall we break, if it is convenient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll save this and give it a new number. But, yes, again it should be under seal. Take a look at the pages I referred to earlier, 65 ter 9 -- I forgot the number. But think about whether we can use it. We'll break. What's the number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D800, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll break for a bit more than 20 minutes, and we'll resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us wrap up with this incident. Now, tell us, please, was this sketch of yours an official part of the on-site report -- investigation report, or, rather, was that the only sketch that was attached to the report?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was the only sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else make a sketch, and does it differ from yours?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that I made the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it is part of this report, and it served as a sketch of the site, the impact site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Would you allow me just to take another look at this sketch, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We do have an unsigned version, and maybe it would be a good idea to show you that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Could you keep this one, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. That's 1802, P1802. Would you like it to be rotated by 180 degrees so that we can have the north where it should be?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we rotate it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we see that the street is between the two buildings. This is the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, where we see the number, the stamp number?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please draw a line through the middle of that street.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I just say something? I cannot recall precisely every detail of this on-site investigation, so that my answers will not be of the quality desired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can this sketch be of the quality desired, the sketch that served the investigators to draw their conclusions? What kind of conclusions could they draw, in view of the fact that the north is marked the way it is here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they could -- what conclusions they could draw. That was really up to them, not up to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please take a look at number 2, Witness. How can it be that the shell landed by the very edge of the building from the north, coming in from the north?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: The shell could land -- could have landed like this, coming from the east, not from the north. In that case, there wouldn't have been any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do we see the east now, the cardinal point of east? Now, please take a look at the way you indicated east and north. There isn't even a 90-degree angle there between them.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can -- I can do that, I can mark it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, please use a green pen, and maybe you can indicate.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me indicate where the east is [marks] in relation to what I marked as north. Now here we see that they are correlated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now please draw a line through the middle of this street, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, in green.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Here it is [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the left we see one building, on the right-hand side another building, and then behind the building there's a courtyard; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the building that we see lying horizontally as we see it here, it lies almost east-west; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, actually, this building, its orientation is south-east, approximately, south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what your vantage point was when you took the photos? Do you know where you were?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please now mark Lukavica here on this sketch.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is to the east, and bearing south-east. Lukavica is a large area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, could you mark the barracks, the military installations? Would you mark that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was a student in Lukavica, and I'm very familiar with Lukavica. It's an entire complex of buildings, of barracks. They're all one next to the other. It's one compound. There are roads between them and then the next barracks lies, so there's a whole series of barracks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you mark it, then, please. Mark the Lukavica area in relation to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is -- this part would be Lukavica [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, no, this is Dobrinja still. But could you just indicate the direction of Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please tender this? If the witness can just date and sign it, although I see we have it. But perhaps because of these green markings, we should have a new exhibit adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D801, under seal. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 09617, page 26.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1710, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this photo? Have you taken it or -- and what does it depict?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this photograph, but I believe that a colleague of mine took it. I'm not actually sure whether it was me or Sead Besic, a crime investigation technician, who actually took this photo. And it depicts the spot -- the point of impact of a mortar shell marked with number 1, and then a street plan of Sarajevo was placed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, in other words, you did use a street plan of Sarajevo or a map of Sarajevo when you made this sketch?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, this is part of the investigation, and the portion that had to do with the placing of the map and the compass there is something that the investigators did. Mr. Sabljica and Zlatko Medjedovic, they are the ones who are responsible for that. I only took photos. And I'm not even sure that I was the one who took this photo. It could have been my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, then, what is the direction of this edge, the edge of this playground?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the playground edge is approximately south-east. That's the direction, south-easterly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have page 3 [as interpreted] of this document, please. I805 [as interpreted], 23, page 23. Page 23. The transcript says "3," but that's an error. Page 23, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, because that's the place where we conducted the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you now please tell us what we see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the photo shows the place where mortar shells landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- could you show the cardinal point north, Witness?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about these buildings; how are they oriented in relation to the playground? What is their orientation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The northerly direction should be -- can I use the marker, the pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can use the e-pen.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I look at the map of the city, and using the map, I would say that this would be approximately the orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we can see a path -- a pedestrian path there; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it runs north-south?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the pedestrian path does not run north-south purely. It's a bit to the north-east, approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D -- or, rather, I would like to tender this into evidence. It was admitted as a P exhibit, but with these markings it should be a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have to emphasise at this moment you have to be more efficient in your cross-examination. You are dwelling on still the north-east on these pictures and maps. I think you already made a point, and you could have moved on, on other points, earlier on. We'll admit this, this page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D802, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then we will move on to a new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- oh, we lost it without dating it, but it doesn't matter because it's in the transcript. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll move on to the next incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that there is no other sketch in this entire investigation report, we have to conclude that there was no additional sketch; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if we did have another sketch, we would take a look at it. Now, let's move on to the Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva Trg. Tell us, please, when did you arrive on site there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived at the incident site 10 days after the incident, itself, and that's because there was intense shelling and we were prevented from getting there earlier without jeopardising our lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the word "tekbir" means?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't see what that has to do with anything in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, did you ever hear of Operation Tekbir?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 15th of June, a large operation was launched, a 1st Corps operation, the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army 1st Corps? This was on the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a police officer. I was not an army member, I was a policeman, so I did not know what the Supreme Command of the BH Army was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it was preparing for the operation earlier on, but on the 15th, the big operation began. How can you not know that when all the three divisions were used in this operation, this major offensive, and -- the 12th, 14th and 16th Divisions took part in it. Do you know that it was launched then, on the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's take a look at 65 ter 09791. It may have been admitted previously. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P431, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it is under seal, it should not be broadcast in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, are you familiar with this official note?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that an on-site investigation was carried out 10 days after the incident.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a map, Map 1D2636. 1D2636.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this map, and can you mark on it the incident site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the Alipasino Polje neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has already confirmed the location of the incident site for this incident, and he confirmed the Prosecution's map showing the location. Perhaps Mr. Karadzic could ask his questions based on that map. It might speed things up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, why not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the Defence has the right to test the credibility and reliability of the witness. For that reason, we thought we might use another map. No hard feelings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark precisely on this map where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot mark the incident site exactly on this map because the buildings on Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva are not plotted into this map. This is a very rough map. This is a general map showing the street and just a few buildings. Not all the buildings are shown in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right. In this map, can you then -- or do you agree that viewing from left to right, we see Standard, Faro Electro [phoen] and Vranica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then "UPI," "Zora," "TAM"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then "ZGP Bosna," "UP Distribution Centre," "Rumenka," [phoen] "TAM," then "Energoinvest," "RMK Wire Factory," and so on and so forth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you call this whole area, this belt, a residential zone, or is it a purely industrial zone without a single residential building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This belt is an industrial zone. However, it is not purely industrial. There are some parts where there are demolished buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between Mese Selimovica and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the names of the streets?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you repeat the last part of your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please use a pencil and mark the whole length of Safeta Zajke Street and then Mese Selimovica, and encircle the area that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Safeta Zajke Street [marks]. It stretches along the length of the city. And below here is Mese Selimovica Street [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is Stupsko Brdo, which was also held by the Serbs [as interpreted] throughout the whole war, and it was important?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a mistake in the transcript. They were not held by the Serbs, the name of Stupsko Brdo, and it was important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the Serbs did not hold it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you're not able to mark the incident site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva. In the map, it's below "PTT Engineering," somewhere in the middle of the Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva. However, this map is not a detailed one, so I cannot mark it precisely. So, roughly speaking, around the middle of this square.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you also see the TV Radio-Television building, the Novi Grad Assembly building and the Survey Institute?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are on the right-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark Majdanska Street --

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Majdanska Street [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Safeta Hadzica Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the incident place on Safeta Zajke, and with which street does it intersect?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think with Dolacka Street, roughly speaking. I'm not quite sure. Anyway, either with Esada Midzica or Dolacka Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please mark it there between the two streets.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that's one incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another one happened near Bitumenka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, here it is closer to PTT Engineering building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One is on TV.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One is on Majdanska Street, behind the RTV building, the Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know which kind of military installations were based in the Survey Institute?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were survey maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. Was there anything else of a military nature housed in the institute?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the police station was here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The police station was above the Municipal Assembly building, or, rather, on the hill above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the south of it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see Geteova Street, and do you agree that it used to be called Cetinjska Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Geteova Street was always called Geteova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How about Cetinjska and Klare Cetkin Streets?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that these streets existed under those names, but I don't know exactly where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to use the transcript and not use other notes. Do you know what the RMK Wire Factory manufactured?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know that shells were being marked within this whole complex?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the date and the number 166.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to put the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the date and number 166 so that it doesn't have to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you said you couldn't exactly mark the area where the incident the 16th of June, 1995, took place, but could you roughly circle the area which you said it's below the PTT Engineering and somewhere in the middle of the street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put "16" and "6."

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you see Geteova Street. You'll need this map later for marking, but can you mark Geteova Street now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be saved as Exhibit D803.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 13564, 65 ter, please. This is a Prosecution map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, is number 15 the incident site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is number 2 Bitumenka?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is number 20 the PTT Engineering building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a little patience, please. How was it stated in the report concerning the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, the shell came from the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Directly from the west or maybe north-west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: West, north-west, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if it came from the west or north-west, the trajectory does not go through the PTT, but it goes either through Bitumenka building or the student dormitory. Can you encircle the student dormitory section in this map?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I can see them [marks]. I have encircled the dormitory with the colour blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the "Oslobodjenje" building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. How shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Encircle it and put the number 3.

utterances.speaker: KDZ166 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
